assessmentOptions.label: Medical History
assessmentOptions.clue: Known CHF — takes furosemide daily. Missed doses this week.

cpap.message: CPAP applied. Work of breathing decreased.

nitro_paste.message: Nitroglycerin paste applied — titratable afterload reduction with CPAP.

fluid_bolus.message: Patient becomes more dyspneic. SpO2 drops to 78%.

albuterol.message: Wheezing slightly improved — pulmonary edema worsening.

deterioration.message: Patient in severe respiratory failure. SpO2 72%.

protocolInsight.title: Not All SOB Is Asthma
protocolInsight.body: Bilateral rales with hypertension and CHF history point to pulmonary edema — not bronchospasm. CPAP and nitroglycerin paste are first-line, not albuterol or sublingual nitro under the CPAP mask.

dispatchNotes: Patient reports worsening breathing overnight. Has not slept flat in weeks.

appearance: Sitting upright on edge of bed.

assessmentOptions.label: Medical History
assessmentOptions.clue: Orthopnea — sleeps on 4 pillows. Leg swelling x 2 weeks.

assessmentOptions.label: ECG
assessmentOptions.clue: Left ventricular hypertrophy pattern. No acute changes.

nitroglycerin.message: Nitroglycerin SL given. BP 164/88. Dyspnea slightly improved.

nitro_paste.message: Nitroglycerin paste applied. Ongoing afterload reduction.

fluid_bolus.message: Fluid bolus given — patient becomes more dyspneic. SpO2 80%.

protocolInsight.title: Orthopnea Is a Clue
protocolInsight.body: Sleeping on multiple pillows is a classic sign of CHF decompensation. Mild cases may respond to nitroglycerin SL or paste before escalating to CPAP. Once CPAP is on, switch to paste — SL is unreliable under the mask.

dispatchNotes: Patient audibly wheezing per caller. History of lung disease unknown.

appearance: No fever, skin warm and dry.

assessmentOptions.label: Lung Sounds
assessmentOptions.clue: Wheezing AND bilateral rales — mixed picture.

assessmentOptions.label: Medical History
assessmentOptions.clue: CHF and COPD on chart — non-compliant with diuretics.

nitroglycerin.message: Nitroglycerin SL with CPAP on — hypotension and no reliable SL absorption.

nitro_paste.message: Nitroglycerin paste applied. BP 158/86 — titratable with CPAP.

albuterol.message: Wheezing slightly better — but rales worsening. SpO2 80%.

fluid_bolus.message: Fluid bolus — patient becomes more dyspneic. SpO2 76%.

deterioration.message: Treated as asthma. Pulmonary edema worsening — SpO2 70%.

perfect_save.title: Patient Stabilized
perfect_save.message: Wheezing with rales correctly identified as CHF.

wrong_protocol.title: Critical Miss
wrong_protocol.message: Wheezing led to wrong pathway. Patient crashing.

protocolInsight.title: Wheezing Can Occur in CHF
protocolInsight.body: Cardiogenic pulmonary edema can produce wheezing — 'cardiac asthma.' Many providers see wheezing and choose asthma. Look for rales, edema, and hypertension together. With CPAP on, use nitroglycerin paste — not SL under the mask.

dispatchNotes: Chest pain with shortness of breath. Diaphoretic. History of heart failure.

assessmentOptions.label: Medical History
assessmentOptions.clue: Known CHF and prior MI. Non-compliant with medications.

assessmentOptions.label: 12-Lead ECG
assessmentOptions.clue: No STEMI. Diffuse ST depression — demand ischemia pattern possible.

twelve_lead.message: 12-lead obtained — no STEMI. Demand ischemia pattern noted.

cardiac_monitor.message: Monitor applied. Tachycardia with frequent PVCs.

cpap.message: CPAP applied. Work of breathing improved.

nitroglycerin.message: Nitroglycerin SL with CPAP in place — BP falls to 132/68. Chest pressure unchanged.

nitro_paste.message: Nitroglycerin paste applied. Chest pressure easing with CPAP.

fluid_bolus.message: Fluid bolus — pulmonary edema worsening. SpO2 79%.

deterioration.message: STEMI not ruled out. CHF decompensation with ischemia worsening.

perfect_save.title: Patient Stabilized

protocolInsight.title: Rule Out STEMI First
protocolInsight.body: Chest pain with CHF history requires a 12-lead before focusing on pulmonary edema treatment. Once CPAP is on, nitroglycerin paste — not SL — provides titratable afterload reduction without fighting the mask.

dispatchNotes: Found in severe distress. Was on home CPAP. Now unresponsive to family.

assessmentOptions.label: Medical History
assessmentOptions.clue: End-stage CHF. Was tachycardic at 130 before bradycardia.

assessmentOptions.label: ECG
assessmentOptions.clue: Sinus bradycardia — was tachycardic 10 minutes ago per family.

cardiac_monitor.message: Monitor applied — bradycardia with frequent ectopy.

notify_facility.message: Cardiogenic shock alert transmitted to receiving.

cpap.message: CPAP applied in shock — patient deteriorating. SpO2 74%.

fluid_bolus.message: Fluid bolus in cardiogenic shock — pulmonary edema worsening. SpO2 70%.

perfect_save.title: Patient Stabilized
perfect_save.message: Shock recognized. Appropriate escalation en route.

delayed_treatment.title: Patient Deteriorating
delayed_treatment.message: Standard CHF treatment applied to shock patient.

wrong_protocol.title: Critical Miss
wrong_protocol.message: Bradycardia after tachycardia missed. Patient in arrest.

protocolInsight.title: Beyond Standard CHF
protocolInsight.body: When CHF progresses to cardiogenic shock — hypotension, bradycardia after tachycardia, altered perfusion — standard CPAP and nitroglycerin are contraindicated. Escalate to shock protocol immediately.
